title: Rethinking Anonymity Claims in Synthetic Data Generation: A Model-Centric Privacy Attack Perspective
abstract: arXiv:2601.22434v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Training generative machine learning models to produce synthetic tabular data has become a popular approach for enhancing privacy in data sharing. As this typically involves processing sensitive personal information, releasing either the trained model or generated synthetic datasets can still pose privacy risks. Yet, recent research, commercial deployments, and privacy regulations like the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) largely assess anonymity at the level of an individual dataset.   In this paper, we rethink anonymity claims about synthetic data from a model-centric perspective, arguing that meaningful assessments must account for the underlying generative model and be grounded in state-of-the-art privacy attacks. This perspective better reflects real-world deployments, where trained models are often accessible for interaction or querying. translated_title: 重新思考合成数据生成中的匿名性声明：以模型为中心的隐私攻击视角
translated_abstract: 训练生成式机器学习模型来产生合成表格数据已成为增强数据共享隐私的一种流行方法。由于这通常涉及处理敏感的个人信息，发布训练好的模型或生成的合成数据集仍然可能带来隐私风险。然而，近期的理论研究、商业部署以及《通用数据保护条例》（GDPR）等隐私法规，在很大程度上都只是在单个数据集层面评估匿名性。在本文中，我们以模型为中心的视角重新思考关于合成数据的匿名性声明，认为有意义的评估必须考虑底层的生成模型，并建立在最先进的隐私攻击之上。这一视角更好地反映了现实世界的部署情况——即训练好的模型通常可以被访问以进行交互或查询。我们对GDPR中关于个人数据和匿名化的定义进行了解释……
tldr: 该论文主张从以模型为中心的视角重新评估合成数据的匿名性声明，认为隐私评估必须考虑底层生成模型并基于最先进的隐私攻击方法，而非仅在单个数据集层面进行判断。
